editorial:
Imagine being a kid who is scared of everything, especially the dark. You will meet Orion, a young boy whose brain never stops worrying about the worst-case scenario. The movie takes a wild turn when Dark, a giant and friendly creature who represents the night, decides to take Orion on a tour to show him why the night is actually important. It feels like a cozy bedtime story come to life, with a vibe that is both sweet and funny. You get to see the world from a child's perspective, making the adventure feel huge and exciting even though it is mostly about facing your own fears.

The animation is bright and colorful, and the voice acting makes the characters feel real and relatable. One of the best parts is how it handles anxiety without being too heavy, keeping the pace snappy and the jokes landing well. While some parts of the plot are a bit predictable, it is still a heartwarming ride. You should definitely watch this with your kids or anyone who needs a little reminder that it is okay to be afraid. For the best experience, try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Netflix or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for those crisp visuals.
endingExplained: After traveling through the night, Orion realizes that Dark is actually lonely and scared of the light. Orion helps Dark face his own fear, showing that everyone struggles with something. They both learn that fear is just a part of life. In the end, Orion stops letting his worries run his life and becomes a braver person. He maintains his friendship with Dark, and the movie wraps up with a happy, peaceful feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about friendship and overcoming fear.
